unterschrift.text: The Saavedra study, White to move wins. Gold arrow: the pawn's path.

fragen.frage: Why does White play 1. c7 right away?
antworten: It stalemates the black king.
The pawn is right before its goal, and the rook can only disturb it with checks.
On c7 the pawn defends its own king.
fragen.erklaerung: A rook move to d8 fails to the capture cxd8. All Black can do is gain time with checks.

fragen.frage: Why does the king go to c2 now?
antworten: White wants to repeat the position and make a draw.
It wants to defend the pawn on c7 from behind.
From c2 it covers c3 and d2: every further check costs the rook.
fragen.erklaerung: The rook has no safe checks left. Black has to come up with something new.

fragen.frage: Why is 3. c8=Q a mistake here?
antworten: Rc1+ skewers the king on c5 and the queen on c8 along the c-file.
The new queen stalemates the black king.
The rook on d1 can capture the queen right away.
fragen.erklaerung: The king has to get out of check, then the rook captures the queen. With 2. Kc5? the king stood on the wrong file.

unterschrift.text: , White to move: draw. Gray arrow: the pin. Red: the pawn on c7 must not move.

fragen.frage: Why can't White make progress here?
antworten: The white king has no squares left.
Black threatens mate on the a-file.
The rook on d7 pins the pawn on c7 to the king on b7.
fragen.erklaerung: The pawn must not move as long as it shields its own king. If the king steps away, the rook captures the pawn.

unterschrift.text: , White to move. Red arrow: the planned rook sacrifice on c4.

fragen.frage: Why does White promote to a rook and not to a queen?
antworten: A rook on c8 is safe from all checks.
After c8=Q comes Rc4+, and after Qxc4 Black is stalemated.
Black could capture a queen on c8 right away.
fragen.erklaerung: The queen on c4 would also cover a2. A rook on c4 does not cover a2, so there is no stalemate.

antworten: Black has no legal move left.
White can promote the c-pawn once more.
The rook on a4 is attacked, and if it moves away, Rc1 mates.
fragen.erklaerung: Double duty for a single rook: it cannot flee and guard the first rank at the same time.

abschnitt.titel: The Réti study: one king route with two goals

unterschrift.text: The Réti study, White to move draws. Red arrow: the h-pawn seems unstoppable. Gold arrow: the path of the white pawn.

fragen.frage: Why does the king go to g7?
antworten: From there it covers the promotion square h1.
It approaches the h-pawn and its own c-pawn at the same time.
It wants to stalemate the black king.
fragen.erklaerung: A diagonal king move counts as much as a straight one, but it covers two directions. That way both goals stay within reach.

unterschrift.text: , Black to move. Gold arrows: on f4 the king stands in the square, on d6 it defends the pawn.

fragen.frage: Why is the king move to e5 so strong?
antworten: From e5 it reaches f4 in the square of the h-pawn or d6 next to the c-pawn.
It puts the black king in zugzwang and wins at once.
It already defends the pawn on c6.
fragen.erklaerung: If Black captures on c6, the king catches the h-pawn. If the h-pawn runs, the king supports the c-pawn.

antworten: From a7 the bishop covers the square h8.
It attacks the bishop on d4; if that bishop captures on a7, it leaves the long diagonal.
It keeps its own king safe from bishop checks.
fragen.erklaerung: After Bxa7 and h7, no black unit can reach h8 anymore. An immediate h7, on the other hand, Black answers with e4.

unterschrift.text: , Black to move. Gold: the bishop on d4 as bait. Gray arrow: the black bishop's diagonal, which it blocks.

fragen.frage: Why does White put the bishop en prise on d4?
antworten: It blocks the diagonal: after the capture on d4, the black bishop stays behind an obstacle.
From d4 it covers the square h8 for its own pawn.
After the trade, White is a pawn up.
fragen.erklaerung: Whether bishop or pawn captures on d4: the white king holds the block in place. Then the h-pawn runs through.

abbildungen.unterabschnitt: Two knights need an enemy pawn

antworten: The knight threatens to capture the pawn on h4.
It mates at once.
It takes h7 from the king; Black has to play h3, and Ng6 mates.
fragen.erklaerung: A quiet move puts Black in zugzwang. The pawn that saves Black from stalemate becomes Black's undoing.

fragen.frage: Why is 1. Ng5 a mistake here?
antworten: The knight on g5 can be captured.
Afterwards Black has no legal move and is not in check: stalemate.
Black can escape to g8.
fragen.erklaerung: The same idea as in the position with the pawn, but without a stalemate reserve the zugzwang turns into stalemate.

fragen.frage: Why does Black have no move left here?
antworten: The king is in check and cannot get away.
The queen on e6 pins f6 and covers f5 and f7, h4 covers g5; all other black units are blocked.
Black may not move because White gave check last.
fragen.erklaerung: No check, no legal move: that is stalemate. A few white units are enough, because the black ones lock each other in.
